# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Logon Hardening

Requires CTRL+ALT+DEL before sign-in and removes the network selection from the lock screen.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | CIS v4 Windows 11 L1 — settings taken from IntuneAdmin, values verified against the settings catalog definition. |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Logon_Hardening.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Logon_Hardening.json) |

> Noticeable for users, so announce it: after this policy everyone has to press CTRL+ALT+DEL before the sign-in screen appears. On tablets and 2-in-1s without a keyboard, Windows uses the Windows button plus power instead. The wording in the setting name is inverted: "Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL" on Disabled means that it is in fact required. Two additions on the sign-in screen: the user's email address is no longer shown there, and connected users are not enumerated. Both take half of a sign-in attempt — the user name — away from whoever sees the screen.
